sources.title: Sobre o País
sources.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estatística de São Tomé e Príncipe (INE)
sources.rights: No reuse license identified; restoration-only. No page body redistributed.
sources.inspected_fact: INE says the 21 November 1980 Administrative Division Law defined seven districts (six on São Tomé and one on Príncipe) with district municipal chambers; it also states that Príncipe currently has autonomous-region status. This is current page content inspected 2026-10-05; the specific legal text itself was not independently retrieved.

sources.title: Découpage Administratif
sources.publisher: Gabon Ministry of Interior, Security and Decentralization
sources.retrieval_method: Official page rendered by the web search/open service; direct HTTP retrieval from this worker environment timed out.
sources.rights: No reuse license identified; no page body redistributed.
inspected_facts: The page table is headed Province, chef-lieu, departments, districts, governor.
Haut-Ogooué lists eleven departments, and all eleven source features scoped here are in that official listing after lossless accent/punctuation normalization.
Ogooué-Ivindo lists Ivindo, Zadié, Mvoung and Lopé, matching the four scoped source units after diacritic/punctuation normalization.

Ogooué-Lolo lists Lolo Bouénguidi, Mulundu, Lombo Bouénguidi and Offoué Onoyé. The scoped source label Mouloundou does not normalize to Mulundu and remains an unresolved alias/name discrepancy; the other three scoped labels are supported by spelling variants.

The page contains an eight-department listing for Ngounié while a separate Ministry territorial-count table reports nine. Because those public summaries conflict and their dates/vintages differ from the 2018 source geometry, this packet does not infer nationwide completeness from the counts.
sources.source_hash_limit: No byte-exact hash is available for the rendered official HTML because its origin server timed out on direct retrieval. Restoration URL and specific source page/date are preserved; do not treat the web rendering as retained original bytes.

sources.title: Découpage Territorial
sources.publisher: Gabon Ministry of Interior, Security and Decentralization
sources.retrieval_method: Official page rendered by the web search/open service; direct HTTP retrieval from this worker environment timed out.
sources.rights: No reuse license identified; no page body redistributed.
inspected_facts: The table reports 9 provinces and 48 departments; counts for the three relevant provinces are Haut-Ogooué 11, Ogooué-Ivindo 4 and Ogooué-Lolo 4.
It names Law No. 14/96 of 15 April 1996 as the territorial reorganization basis.

The official aggregate's 48 departments differs from the 49 features in geoBoundaries GAB ADM2. It is a 2016 count versus 2018-representative source data and does not identify which national unit explains the difference.

sources.title: Estrutura da População — RGPH 2012
sources.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estatística de São Tomé e Príncipe (INE)
sources.rights: No reuse license identified; restoration-only. Temporary downloaded bytes were inspected then omitted from the repository.

inspected_pages.fact: Administrative organization lists six São Tomé districts (Água Grande, Mé-Zóchi, Cantagalo, Caué, Lembá, Lobata) and an autonomous region (Ilha do Príncipe); the report says Príncipe has held autonomous-region status since 1996. It distinguishes district municipalities from the regional government.

The report describes the country as an archipelago with the two main islands, and separately notes other small islands. This cautions against inferring national land/islet completeness from the two-feature ADM1 source.
